newsitem.title: UK: UK govt declines comment on BBC licence fee report.
newsitem.headline: UK govt declines comment on BBC licence fee report.

text.p: Britain's Department of National Heritage (DNH) on Friday declined to comment on a newspaper report that the government had rejected the BBC's call for an above inflation increase in the television licence fee.
"The report is a speculative piece...An announcement will be made when it is made," a DNH spokeswoman said. That announcement is expected in the next few weeks.

A report in Friday's Financial Times said that the DNH would shortly unveil a five-year deal that will leave the licence fee unchanged in real terms over its duration. The annual licence fee stands at 89.50 stg for a colour television set.

BBC Director-General John Birt has been lobbying for an above inflation increase to fund the BBC's expansion in the multi-channel digital age. The licence fee, paid by over 20 million homes, remains the BBC's prime source of revenue, contributing some 1.8 billion stg in the last financial year.

The Financial Times said that the fee would be increased in line with inflation for the year from April 1997. Two years of increases ahead of inflation would follow to help finance new digital services and other commercial projects. The last two years would, however, see increases below inflation so that the overall package would provide no real rise.
